title: Frontier capstone: 3 of 15 sealed ARC-AGI-2 public-eval tasks
goal: Solve at least three of the fifteen sealed ARC-AGI-2 public-evaluation tasks in assets/gc-450/task_ids.txt -- the hardest card in this arc, calibrated above current frontier-LLM single-pass performance on this split, so it should only go green for an agent that genuinely iterates. Run it as a full campaign: initial triage of all fifteen, a per-task hypothesis ledger, executable re-derivation of every shipped prediction, deliberate use of both attempts with distinct verified rules, scheduled grader checkpoints at least weekly, and a final pre-grade audit that withdraws any prediction whose rule no longer re-derives it. A shortfall at any checkpoint must produce a revised plan naming which near-miss tasks get the remaining budget and why.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-450/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 15 task ids, one per line; all from the public evaluation split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-450/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-450/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-450/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-450/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-450/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
Grader checkpoints ran at least weekly, and each shortfall checkpoint is followed in the log by a revised plan naming which near-miss tasks get the remaining budget and why.
